items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I even asked him once, I said, is it true that Muggsy had recorded with him? And he said, yes. No, I don't know.

ctx.x: I have a note here. He mentioned that there were

three great clarinetists in New Orleans. Piku, Lorenzo Tio, and George Bakke. He didn't think Big Eye Louie was really in the first class. Other people will tell you they think Big Eye was better than Piku and so on. So some of that could be a question of opinion. he thought Dodds wasn't really a first class clarinetist. He was all right. He was only on a couple of his records, maybe four sides or so. I don't know. I even asked him once, I said, is it true that Muggsy had recorded with him? And he said, yes. No,…
He was dead in that two summer.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: Which reminds me once of when we interviewed, you were there, weren't you, Dick? Was that back of the Dream Room, Muggsy Spanier?

ctx.x: So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…
Well, of course, we'll never know what Joe Oliver really sounded like.
